answer: To resist sybil attacks agents must each lock a unique quartz crystal inside a sealed bridge-like container that only opens after a timed cipher challenge is solved on-site. The crystal is photographed at the moment of opening with a live timestamp. An attacker forging many identities must physically source and place distinct quartz pieces in separate containers for every fake, then solve the cipher in real time at each location; the cost grows with the number of aliases because materials and simultaneous physical presence cannot be shared, while an honest agent needs only one setup.
